edition: Issue #008 - Newcastle from wooden spoon to grand final, a boss calls small talk a firing offence, and a burglar proposal ends at the wrong address
tagline: Your 3-minute break. Zero fluff, maximum banter.

stories.headline: Newcastle Knights cap a wooden-spoon-to-grand-final miracle with 12 men
stories.summary: A week after knocking the Warriors out, the side that finished last in 2025 booked an NRL grand final spot by beating premiers Penrith 22-14 despite playing most of the game shorthanded.

body.text: A week after eliminating the NZ Warriors, the Newcastle Knights have booked a place in the NRL grand final, beating regular-season premiers Penrith Panthers 22-14 at Sydney Accor Stadium. The Knights finished with the wooden spoon last season. They had to play most of the game shorthanded after hooker Phoenix Crossland was sent off for a hip-drop tackle on Penrith superstar Nathan Cleary, who was stretchered off with a suspected compound ankle fracture before halftime. No team has ever improved from last on the table to NRL champions in one season; Newcastle have now matched the 2010 Roosters, who traded their spoon for a grand final spot.

A side that finished bottom of the entire competition has just removed two of the fanciest clubs on the way to a grand final, and they did a chunk of it shorthanded, the rugby-league equivalent of running a full service on one wheel. There is officially nothing left for the pre-season party planners to promise the rest of us. And just when the Warriors were that close to a grand final run of their own, they now have the added joy of cheering on the team that knocked them out. Nothing personal, fellas; the ledger is still very much open.

RNZ (27 Sep 2026, from Accor Stadium): Newcastle Knights beat Penrith 22-14 in the NRL preliminary final to reach the grand final against the Sydney Roosters. They finished with the wooden spoon in 2025 and eliminated the NZ Warriors the previous week. Newcastle played most of the game shorthanded after hooker Phoenix Crossland was sent off for a hip-drop challenge that left Penrith Nathan Cleary stretchered off with a suspected compound ankle fracture, likely ruling him out of the Rugby League World Cup and jeopardising his NZ Kiwis involvement. No team has gone from last on the table to NRL champions in one season; the closest parallel is the 2010 Roosters, who reached the grand final from the spoon but lost to St George Illawarra.

stories.headline: Truck driver sacked for lingering small talk with a customer wins $32k
stories.summary: Eric Tillocksingh was fired by Drivers Employment Ltd after a delivery customer felt uncomfortable at him asking do you work from home, a dismissal the Employment Relations Authority ruled unjustified, with the boss calling him a stupid f***ing idiot.

body.text: Truck driver Eric Tillocksingh delivered a furniture shipment to a Christchurch home in June and made small talk with the woman who answered, including asking do you work from home. A customer then complained his flatmate felt extremely uncomfortable, and Drivers Employment Ltd (DEL) sacked him. Now the Employment Relations Authority has ruled the dismissal unjustified due to a flawed process with considerable procedural failures, ordering DEL to pay him $32,448.75, which is $15,000 for humiliation and loss of dignity plus $17,448.75 in lost wages. The authority found the interaction was unlikely to reach the threshold of serious misconduct without other evidence of inappropriate or threatening body language. DEL owner Stuart Biggs has a lengthy history with the ERA through another company he owns.

A man has just been handed $32,000 for the grave workplace sin of being friendly to a customer while making a delivery. Meanwhile the boss chosen method of dispute resolution was to call him a stupid f***ing idiot, a phrase that has, to our knowledge, never once de-escalated a situation. We are all expected to read the room at work, so here is the final ruling: polite small talk during a delivery is a firing offence, while swearing at a staffer and never asking for the doorbell footage is, apparently, just very expensive. One of those two ends in a pay-out, and it is not the small talk.

RNZ (27 Sep 2026, from NZ Herald / Open Justice): The Employment Relations Authority ordered Drivers Employment Ltd to pay truck driver Eric Tillocksingh $32,448.75 ($15,000 for humiliation, loss of dignity and injury to feelings, plus $17,448.75 lost remuneration) after finding his dismissal for lingering during a delivery was unjustified. The complaint said Tillocksingh had asked do you work from home, told the flatmate see you soon and interacted with the dog; he said it was small talk with no malice. Authority member William Fussey found the process flawed with considerable procedural failures, and that DEL never genuinely sought Tillocksingh account nor asked for the doorbell footage cited in the complaint. DEL owner Stuart Biggs has a history with the ERA: his other company Star Moving has previously been ordered to pay tens of thousands in compensation and repeated penalties for an unjustified dismissal.

stories.headline: Burglar steals $2700 ring to propose, returns it devalued by half, then blames a twin
stories.summary: Jarrod Bennett took a ring from a Nelson jeweller because he wanted to propose to his girlfriend, returned it worth half as much, claimed police must have had a twin in mind, and was jailed for just over two years.

body.text: A burglar who stole a $2700 ring from a central Nelson jewellery store says his motives were driven by love. Jarrod Bennett, 26, planned to propose to his girlfriend, and his defence lawyer called the theft spontaneous behaviour. When stopped by police he told them there must have been a twin out there wearing the same clothing. Bennett was sentenced in the Nelson District Court to just over two years in prison for the burglary, part of a spree in which he stole items worth about $8000, including the ring, which he returned but which was by then devalued by half, two new Samsung phones, a gaming console, alcohol and cigarettes. Judge Tony Snell called the thefts brazen and made no reparation order because repayment would take about 16 years. Bennett lawyer said there was no word on the nuptials and the relationship was likely over.

There is a unique level of confidence required to rob a jeweller for a ring to propose, return it slightly used, and still expect the answer to be yes, this is the free-returns approach to romance, the kind of man who treats a marriage proposal like a jumper that does not quite fit. The kicker is the legal strategy: must have been a twin wearing the same clothing. Sir, that is not a defence, that is the opening scene of a very bad comedy. And the punchline is that the ring lost half its value on the way back, the only form of depreciation that also applied to the relationship.

RNZ (27 Sep 2026, from NZ Herald / Open Justice): Jarrod Bennett, 26, was sentenced in the Nelson District Court to two years and two months prison for a burglary spree in March-April 2026 in which he stole items worth about $8000, including a $2700 ring from the Pascoes jewellery store in central Nelson that he returned (devalued by half), two new Samsung phones worth $5010, a $949 gaming console, and alcohol and cigarettes worth $1500-2000 from a dairy. He had admitted robbery by assault and three shoplifting charges; the robbery-by-assault lead charge involved a cashier being smacked on the hand and threatened while trying to stop him. When stopped by police he said there must have been a twin wearing the same clothing. Judge Snell called the thefts brazen, accepted Bennett had an enduring mental illness but found no link to the offending, and made no reparation order because repayment would take about 16 years. Bennett lawyer said the relationship was likely over; he will be eligible for parole after a third of his sentence.
